CATE Simulation Study

Source: vignettes/paper-cate-simulation.Rmd
paper-cate-simulation.Rmd

Overview

This vignette documents the simulation infrastructure for the companion conditional Z-estimation paper listed by citation("RdistNN"). It shows how to use the package-level simulation functions on a small synthetic example. The full Monte Carlo run for the paper main grid is in inst/paper-replication/cate/run.R.

The manuscript repo Cond_Z_Estimation/Codes/Simulations/ now provides the paper-facing orchestration layer on top of these package functions:

  • chunked resumable runs with run manifests and generated run READMEs,
  • the separate nuisance-efficiency launcher, and
  • fixed-\lambda sweep wrappers that write one output folder per \lambda.

To access that script after installing the package:

system.file("paper-replication/cate/run.R", package = "RdistNN")

Data-generating processes

Six DGPs are available via sim_cate_data():

Design tau(x) Propensity Covariate design Notes
dgp1_linear 0.5 x1 - 0.3 x2 logistic iid N(0,I) correctly specified for OLS-interaction
dgp2_nonlinear 0.5 + 0.75 sin(1.5 x1) logistic iid N(0,I) sharper local misspecification design
dgp3_sparse_overlap same as DGP 2 near-boundary except in a tight pocket at x0 iid N(0,I) stress-tests local ESS adaptation
dgp4_clustered same as DGP 2 logistic mixture: 80% N(x0, 0.2²I) + 10% N((4.5,2), 1.25²I) + 10% N((-2.5,-2), 1.25²I) density-adaptivity DGP; DNN shrinks bandwidth at dense x0
dgp5_correlated sin(2x1) + 0.5 x1² steeper logistic N(0,Σ), ρ=0.85; x0=(0.75,0) shape-adaptivity DGP; dnn_oracle_mahal corrects for off-diagonal covariance
dgp6_nuisance_efficiency 0.5 + 0.60 sin(1.5 x1) logistic, simple benchmark nuisance structure iid N(0,I) focused dnn_fullsample versus dnn_crossfit design

All DGPs return oracle nuisances (e_oracle, m0_oracle, m1_oracle, tau_oracle), the paper-facing oracle AIPW score (aipw_oracle), and the legacy Robinson pseudo-outcome (rho_oracle).

dgp <- sim_cate_data("dgp2_nonlinear", n = 300, kx = 2, seed = 42)
head(dgp$data[, c("X1", "X2", "D", "Y", "tau_oracle", "e_oracle")])

Single replicate

sim_cate_one_rep() draws one dataset, fits the DNN Z-estimator using the AIPW score, and returns per-replicate metrics:

tuning_default <- tuning_dnn_paper()
s_default <- tuning_eval(tuning_default, n = 300, kx = 2, k = 1)$s

r <- sim_cate_one_rep(
  n      = 300,
  kx     = 2,
  k      = 1,
  s      = s_default,
  design = "dgp2_nonlinear",
  seed   = 1
)
r
#>       method candidate_id lambda  s  tau_hat     tau0      bias      sq_err
#> 1 dnn_oracle         <NA>     NA 28 1.289072 1.248121 0.0409505 0.001676943

Small Monte Carlo run

The following runs 5 replications per cell over a tiny grid to illustrate the workflow. The manuscript-facing main production grid uses n_reps = 10000, n_vals = c(100, 250, 500, 1000), and the retained designs dgp1_linear, dgp2_nonlinear, dgp4_clustered, and dgp5_correlated. The focused nuisance-efficiency comparison and the fixed-\lambda sweeps are driven from the manuscript repo rather than this package vignette.

raw <- sim_cate_run(
  designs     = c("dgp1_linear", "dgp2_nonlinear"),
  n_vals      = 300L,
  kx_vals     = 2L,
  n_reps      = 5L,
  master_seed = 42L,
  tuning      = tuning_dnn_paper(),
  verbose     = FALSE
)
head(raw)

Parallel execution

sim_cate_run() uses future.apply::future_lapply() for the rep loop when future.apply is installed, and falls back silently to sequential lapply otherwise. The execution backend is controlled by calling future::plan() before the run — no changes to sim_cate_run() are needed.

Personal computer 

library(future)
library(future.apply)

plan(multisession)            # use all local cores
raw <- sim_cate_run(
  designs = "dgp2_nonlinear",
  n_vals  = 500L,
  n_reps  = 50L
)
plan(sequential)              # reset when done

SLURM HPC (array jobs)

For the full paper main grid on a cluster, use the HPC scripts in inst/paper-replication/cate/hpc/. Each SLURM array task runs one (design, n, kx) cell (all 10,000 reps), and uses the cores allocated by --cpus-per-task for within-task rep parallelism.

# Locate the HPC scripts after installing the package:
system.file("paper-replication/cate/hpc", package = "RdistNN")

Workflow on the cluster:

# 1. Install RdistNN on the cluster, then from your working directory:
sbatch /path/to/hpc/submit.sh        # submits 16 array tasks (edit --array if grid changes)

# 2. After all tasks complete, merge the per-cell results:
Rscript /path/to/hpc/merge.R

Results are written to ./results/ by default. Override with export SIM_OUTDIR=/your/path before calling sbatch or merge.R.

Full paper replication (single machine)

To run the full simulation sequentially (or with plan(multisession)) on one machine:

source(system.file("paper-replication/cate/run.R", package = "RdistNN"))

Results are written to ./results/sim_cate_raw.rds and ./results/sim_cate_table.csv in the current working directory.

This package-side script is the manuscript-facing main-grid baseline only. If you want the chunked manuscript output with manifests, the nuisance-efficiency run, or the \lambda-sweep folders, use the launchers in Cond_Z_Estimation/Codes/Simulations/.

Competitor benchmarks

Optional causal-forest, local-linear-forest, naive-OLS, and interaction-OLS benchmarks are in inst/paper-replication/cate/benchmarks.R. In this standalone helper, the GRF routes estimate their nuisance functions internally and record forest_nuisance = "internal". By contrast, the package simulation registry’s causal_forest and llf routes supply oracle outcome and propensity nuisances and record forest_nuisance = "oracle". These benchmarks are not part of the package core; they use requireNamespace() and require optional packages (grf, etc.) listed under Suggests in DESCRIPTION.

system.file("paper-replication/cate/benchmarks.R", package = "RdistNN")
